text: Representation. `sections` is a flat array of pairs (len, ins): len is the span length in the old document; ins is -1 for an unchanged span, otherwise the length of the replacement (insertion (0,n), deletion (n,0), replacement (n,m)). Values built by ChangeSet.of, compose and map go through addSection, which (in this order) drops a section with len 0 and ins <= 0; extends the previous section's len when ins <= 0 equals the previous ins (adjacent unchanged spans merge, adjacent deletions merge: deleting 2-4 and 4-6 of 8 gives the sections (2,-1),(4,0),(2,-1)); adds ins to the previous section when len is 0 and the previous len is 0 (insertions at one point merge); joins into the previous section when forceJoin; otherwise appends. So adjacent replacements stay separate ([[1,'A'],[1,'B'],1]), and a deletion followed by an insertion at its end, or an insertion followed by a deletion at the same point, stay two sections.
hazards: -1 sentinel inside a number array (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:24); any negative ins counts as unchanged in newLength (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:45) and iterChanges (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:410), only ins == -1 in SectionIter.len2/forward2 and mapSet (mirrors/cm6/state/src/change.ts:440, :553, :572)

cost: Memory 2 numbers per section; sections are O(number of changes), independent of document size.

It is combined like an out-of-order run (state.ChangeSet^of.B4/B5): its positions refer to the start document, and an insertion it makes at the same point as an earlier spec lands after that spec's insertion.

text: Arrays, nested to any depth, are processed depth-first in order (empty arrays contribute nothing); every position in every element refers to the document before the whole spec, also after earlier elements changed it; overlapping elements combine (a deletion 0-2 followed by a replacement 1-4 "z" gives [[2],[2,"z"],1]).

Runtime dispatch is duck-typed: Array.isArray, then `instanceof ChangeSet`, else the value is read as an object without checks. A plain ChangeDesc passed as a spec has no `from`, passes the range check (undefined comparisons are false) and is skipped silently; {insert: "x"} without `from` produces a section of length NaN ([[NaN,"x"]], length NaN); string positions "1"/"2" are compared and subtracted as JS values and give sections of numbers; an `insert` that is neither a string nor a Text (7) is used as a Text and breaks later (toJSON throws TypeError). Facts for open question Q12; new facts in question change-s2-q4.

text: Several insertions at the same position in one run merge into one section whose text is the inserts in spec order ("a","b","c" at 1 give [1,[0,"abc"],2]).
In one run, adjacent deletions merge into one section, adjacent replacements stay separate sections, and a deletion followed by an insertion at its end stays two sections (state.ChangeDesc.B1).

A spec whose `from` is before the current run's end flushes the run; runs are combined as `total.compose(set.map(total))`, so positions always refer to the original document, overlapping changes combine, and a later spec's insertion at the same point as an earlier one's lands after it (inserts "a" at 2, "b" at 1, "c" at 2 give [1,[0,"b"],1,[0,"ac"],1]).
cost: Each flush costs a map and a compose over the accumulated set: O(total sections) per out-of-order spec, quadratic for fully reversed input.
